thread:
jen: heads up — multiple customers hitting 502/504s against the hosted inference endpoint since ~13:17 UTC. first reports came from PH-12345 and a few high-traffic tenants. seeing a big spike in gateway errors. :rotating_light:
jen: sample error in support logs: `upstream response code: 502` and `Upstream request timed out after 10s`
ops-bot: alert: envoy_5xx_rate > 3% on svc.hosted-api (13:16-13:22) — firing PagerDuty
maya: oncall eli? can you grab traces and see if this is envoy -> auth -> runtime chain or LB->envoy?
eli: i'm on it. looking at envoy access logs now. early read shows lots of `upstream reset` / `no healthy upstream` to `auth-service` and some `upstream response timeout` to `router-runtime`.
eli: quick grep from envoy logs:
```
# envoy access (abridged)
[13:17:02] "POST /v1/generate" 502 - - - "upstream reset" "upstream_host:10.3.4.12:8080" 0.012
[13:17:03] "POST /v1/generate" 504 - - - "upstream timeout" "upstream_host:10.5.6.90:9000" 10.001
[13:17:05] "POST /v1/generate" 502 - - - "no healthy upstream" "auth-service" 0.000
```
eli: windowed error rate looks correlated with higher latency on auth-service pods (p95 spiked from 40ms -> 2.3s).
sri: any deploys around that time? cause could be new auth change or a GC spike.
maya: deploy-bot shows an auth service rollout completed at 13:10 UTC — version v2.7.2 by @dev-team.
deploy-bot: deploy auth-service v2.7.2 -> success (13:10) :white_check_mark:
jen: #### repro from support (customer-jordan):
1) send token auth request to /v1/generate with long prompt (~8k chars)
2) intermittent 502 with `upstream reset`
3) curl example they used:
```
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"<very long prompt>","max_tokens":1024}'
```
eli: interesting — long prompt causes bigger payload to auth-check path (we do token introspect on request body size?), our auth-service scales per request throughput and seems to get saturated. v2.7.2 added a synchronous token enrichment call that increases CPU per request.
sri: load profile: a few tenants sending batched long requests at the same time — pushes auth pods to CPU throttling -> readiness flapping -> envoy marks them unhealthy -> 502s.
maya: immediate mitigation options:
- rollback auth v2.7.2 to v2.7.1 (fast)
- increase envoy route timeout and retry policy temporarily (makes user wait longer but avoids immediate 502s)
- scale up auth-service replicas / vertical autoscale (short-term)
- route heavy customers to dedicated-capacity (longer term)

eli: i'm going to roll auth back now (canary is at 3 pods, 2 unhealthy). rolling back should restore readiness and healthy upstreams.
eli: rolling back to v2.7.1 -> kicking off now.
deploy-bot: rollback auth-service to v2.7.1 -> started (13:29)
eli: monitor: pinging envoy health and auth endpoints, watch p95 and 5xx rate.
jen: contacting customers with repro steps and asking for timestamped request-ids. leaving a support note: "we're investigating, temporary mitigation in progress (rollback)."
customer-jordan: thanks — we can delay heavy jobs, will hold off for 15m. sending sample request-ids now.
eli: rollback finished, pods back to ready count. deploy-bot: rollback auth-service to v2.7.1 -> success (13:34) :white_check_mark:
eli: post-rollback metrics: auth p95 returned to ~60ms, envoy 5xx rate dropping to baseline.
sri: re-check ingress LB (nginx) timeouts — nginx had 10s proxy_read_timeout, envoy had 10s route_timeout. we should increase route timeout to 30s for long requests and add retries for 502/504 where safe.
maya: agreed — but be careful: increasing timeouts too much may backpressure runtime and increase billable token compute time. propose temporary 30s on /v1/generate and revisit permanent config.
jen: support note updated, telling customers we rolled back auth deploy and recommended clients retry. attaching ticket PH-12345 for tracking.
eli: follow-ups:
- ops: add circuit-breaker metrics + alert for auth pod readiness flapping (sri)
- platform: add a deploy guard for sync token-enrichment (maya)
- dev: optimize token enrichment path for truncated payloads (dev-team)
- support: ask customers to include `X-Request-Id` on retries (jen)

sri: leaving a small retro: canary was too small and didn't catch CPU regression. we should increase canary size for auth and add load test with long-prompt profiles.
jen: will update the incident ticket and escalate to postmortem if we see recurrence. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident resolved (13:50) — postmortem required if recurrence within 7d.
jen: closing thread for now. will re-open if customers see further 502s. :lock:
